sections.h2: Ways to sell a Rosemount house
sections.html:
The Dakota County paperwork below applies on every route, and three are common in a city like this one.

  • An agent listing suits a ready house and a calendar that allows for showings.
  • A sale handled without an agent leaves the disclosure, certificate of value and well disclosure to the seller.
  • An as-is cash purchase fits a rental, an estate property or a house that needs more work than the owner wants to do.

Whichever route you take, write down material facts for the buyer, learn whether the parcel is abstract or Torrens, and have the closing agent send the deed, well disclosure and certificate of value together.

Twenty miles south of Saint Paul, Rosemount marks the southern fringe of the metro in Dakota County. Growth here has been fast: the July 1, 2025 estimate is 31,881 residents, 24.3 percent above the 2020 base of 25,651. Rosemount is a city of owners. About 87.4 percent of homes are owner-occupied, and 91.5 percent of residents stayed put through the prior year.

The median owner-occupied home is worth $424,100, owners with a mortgage pay $2,266 a month, and owners with no mortgage pay $796. Median gross rent is $1,640 and median household income is $129,625. There are 9,924 households averaging 2.77 people.

U.S. Highway 52, Minnesota Highways 3 and 55, and County Road 42 are four of the main routes, and the average commute is 28.1 minutes, so buyers weigh drive times to Saint Paul, Minneapolis and Dakota County job centers. Independent School District 196, the Rosemount-Apple Valley-Eagan district, serves the city.

sections.h2: A step-by-step order for a quick Rosemount sale
sections.html: Begin by finding out whether your parcel is abstract or Torrens, since that tells the closing agent what to search. If the house is rented, call City Hall about the rental license and gather the tenant's lease. Write down every material fact you know about the house for the buyer. Check for wells on the property, because every transfer deed needs either a well certificate or a printed statement about wells. Pick a buyer and agree on a closing date, then ask the closing agent to send the deed, the well disclosure and the certificate of value together. At the Hastings office the deed is recorded, and you should expect the originals back within one to two weeks if the package goes by mail.

A direct cash purchase removes showings, open houses and the wait for a buyer's lender to approve a loan. It does not remove the paperwork. You still give the written disclosure, the deed still needs a well statement, and any sale over $3,000 still needs a certificate of value. What you gain is control over the closing date and freedom from repair requests. What you give up is some of the price an open-market buyer might pay, so compare the offer with what a listing would net after repairs, commissions and the months you would carry the house.

sections.h2: Rental license for a Rosemount house
sections.html:
The City Code requires a rental dwelling license under Title 9-8-4, and the housing official may inspect the property under Title 9-8-8. The city's application asks whether the building is a single-family home, duplex, townhome or multi-family structure, and whether the license is new or a renewal.

  • An owner who rents out properties in other Minnesota cities must list them on the form.
  • A false statement on the application can lead to suspension or revocation.
  • The application lists a fee of $100 per unit when mailed, so call City Hall at 651-322-2024 for the current amount.

For a house sold with a tenant inside, ask City Hall what happens to the license. City Hall is at 2875 145th Street West, and the city's website is rosemountmn.gov.

The road from sales data to a final tax bill takes more than three years. Each year's assessment looks at sales from the twelve months ending September 30 and uses a January 2 market value, which sets the tax payable in the following year. Notices go to every owner in March, and the appeal window runs March through May.

Once the county board adjourns in June, state law bars Assessing Services from changing that year's value. What remains is a Minnesota Tax Court petition, which has an April 30 deadline in the year the tax is payable. The county takes service of petitions at taxpetitions@co.dakota.mn.us or in person in Hastings.

Gather recent sales of similar houses if you plan to question next year's value, and call Assessing Services at 651-438-4200.

sections.h2: What Dakota County needs to record a Rosemount deed
sections.html:
Recording for Dakota County happens at Property Taxation and Records, 1590 Highway 55, Hastings. The office takes deeds at an appointment or through the mail, and a mailed package needs a cover letter, a stamped return envelope and a daytime phone number. Expect the originals back within one to two weeks.

  • The county lists a $46 fee for an abstract document, plus a $5 conservation fee on instruments where deed tax was paid.
  • Card payments for recordings carry a 2.49 percent service charge.
  • Every transfer deed needs a well disclosure certificate, or one of two statements about wells printed on the deed.

Most Dakota County land is abstract property, which means a title company searches the records at sale. Torrens property instead has a certificate of title. The county's property search shows which type applies to your parcel. Dakota County staff will not help fill in legal forms, so rely on a closing agent or an attorney.

sections.h2: The certificate of real estate value
sections.html:
Minn. Stat. 272.115 requires a certificate of value for any sale over $3,000. The seller, buyer or an agent files it with the Dakota County auditor as the deed is presented, and it reports financing terms and nets out personal property sold along with the house.

The same section blocks homestead classification in the years after a sale when no certificate was filed, so ask your closing agent to confirm it goes in with the deed.

faqs.q: Do I need a rental license to sell a house I have been renting out in Rosemount?
faqs.a: The license applies to operating a rental, so ask City Hall at 651-322-2024 what to do with it when the house changes hands. Rosemount's Title 9-8-4 requires the license, and the housing official can inspect under Title 9-8-8.

faqs.q: Can I still appeal my Dakota County assessment after the county board meets?
faqs.a: Not through the county, since state law bars changes to the value once the board adjourns in June. A Tax Court petition stays possible until April 30 of the payable year.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for a Rosemount house?
faqs.a: Dakota County Property Taxation and Records in Hastings records it. You can book an appointment, or mail the deed, the fees, a cover letter and a self-addressed stamped envelope to 1590 Highway 55.

faqs.q: What is a well disclosure on a Minnesota deed?
faqs.a: Dakota County wants to know about wells on every parcel that changes hands. The deed travels with a completed certificate and fee, or with a printed sentence saying the seller knows of no wells or that nothing has changed since the last certificate.

faqs.q: When do Dakota County property tax statements arrive?
faqs.a: Proposed statements go out in November and the final statements follow in March. The first half is due in May and the second half in October.
